The Vendetta Gazette

Vol. XX • August 24, 2026 • “All the Blood That’s Fit to Print” • Two Cents (If You’re Still Alive to Pay)

★ TERRITORY GAINS THIS WEEK ★ Wu-Tang           +165 turfs
Charle Reborn     +1 turf

Wu-Tang, The Unstoppable Juggernaut, Devours Sir Caprice Root and Branch

One Hundred and Sixty-Five Turfs Seized; One Man's Empire Reduced to Rubble and Recrimination; The Iron Fist Shows Mercy to Absolutely Nobody By Our Man in the Trenches, Ignatius P. Flambeau

Last week, dear readers, this correspondent promised himself — and his long-suffering editor — that he would cease beginning every front-page dispatch with a superlative tribute to the seemingly boundless territorial appetites of one Wu-Tang, the Iron Fist of the East Side. That promise, it grieves us to report, has been broken with spectacular and entirely unapologetic swiftness.

For the third consecutive week, Wu-Tang has descended upon Vendetta City's map like a plague of extremely well-organised locusts, annexing one hundred and sixty-five turfs in seven days and directing every last one of his one hundred and sixty-six territorial assaults at a single, apparently helpless target: the unfortunate soul known to the underworld as Sir Caprice. One hundred and sixty-six captures. One hundred and sixty-six times the Iron Fist's henchmen, bouncers, and fearsome enforcers came knocking at Sir Caprice's doors. One hundred and sixty-six times, those doors were kicked clean off their hinges.

Sir Caprice — once spoken of in certain downtown saloons as a man of considerable territorial clout — has surrendered one hundred and sixty-five turfs across the week, a systematic dismantlement so thorough and so methodical that city cartographers have reportedly retired the man's name from their working maps altogether. Whether Sir Caprice himself remains among the living and the propertied, or whether he now wanders the gutters of Vendetta City with nothing but his pride and a very bad memory, this correspondent could not confirm at press time. What is confirmed is that Wu-Tang did not merely raid the man — he conquered him, block by bleeding block, without so much as a curtsey of diplomacy.

And yet — and here is the detail that keeps this reporter awake at night — the Iron Fist was not satisfied with conquest alone. Wu-Tang's crews also conducted eighty-three raids upon Sir Caprice's dwindling holdings this week, stripping cash and weaponry from the wreckage of each fallen turf before the smoke had even cleared. The total haul of the week's raiding activity across Vendetta City reached sixty-one thousand dollars in cash and nearly sixty-one thousand in arms. One shudders to imagine what Wu-Tang intends to do with it all.

Claude the Quiet Builds His Walls Whilst Others Fight

Seven Hundred and Fifty-Eight Fresh Recruits; A General Who Prepares, Not Merely Postures By Our City Desk Correspondent

Whilst the headlines this week belong — as they have for three weeks running — to Wu-Tang's relentless campaign of territorial expansion, the sharp-eyed student of Vendetta City's criminal geography would do well to cast their gaze southward toward the quieter but considerably more purposeful operations of Claude, the man your correspondent has taken to calling the Architect of the Slow Siege.

Claude added a staggering seven hundred and fifty-eight garrison units to his organisation this week, bringing his total standing army to one thousand, five hundred and thirty-one souls — a number which rivals the population of certain respectable townships in this great nation. Claude lost one turf to the enterprising Charle Reborn, it is true, but a man who responds to a territorial nibble by nearly doubling the size of his army is not a man who is panicking. He is a man who is preparing. For what, precisely, this newspaper does not yet know. But we intend to find out, and we strongly advise our readers to keep their hats on.

Claude also conducted nineteen raids upon the city's more vulnerable inhabitants this week, proving that the Architect does not merely build — he also collects, methodically and without fanfare, the resources that will one day fund whatever grand design he has scrawled upon the walls of his headquarters.

Charle Reborn Makes His Mark — One Turf At a Time

A Newcom
